ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals AC and BD of the rhombus ABCD intersect at point O. Point E is a point on side AD, and $OD = OE$. If $AC = 8$ and $BD = 6$, then what is the length of AE?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw ON $\perp$ AD at point N,\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ OD=$\frac{1}{2}$BD=3, OA=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=4, AC$\perp$BD,\\
$\therefore$ AD=$\sqrt{OA^{2}+OD^{2}}$=5,\\
$\because$ OD=OE, ON$\perp$AD at point N,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OND=90$^\circ$, DN=EN,\\
$\therefore$ S$_{\triangle AOD}$=$\frac{1}{2}$AD·ON=$\frac{1}{2}$OD·OA,\\
$\therefore$ 5ON=12,\\
$\therefore$ ON=$\frac{12}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ DN=$\sqrt{OD^{2}-ON^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-\left(\frac{12}{5}\right)^{2}}=\frac{9}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ DE=2DN=$\frac{18}{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ AE=AD-DE=5-$\frac{18}{5}=\boxed{\frac{7}{5}}$.

Therefore, $AD=\sqrt{OA^{2}+OD^{2}}=5$. Since $OD=OE$ and $ON\perp AD$ at point N, $\angle OND=90^\circ$ and $DN=EN$. Also, $S_{\triangle AOD}=\frac{1}{2}AD\cdot ON=\frac{1}{2}OD\cdot OA$, so $5ON=12$, hence $ON=\frac{12}{5}$. Then $DN=\sqrt{OD^{2}-ON^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-\left(\frac{12}{5}\right)^{2}}=\frac{9}{5}$. Therefore, $DE=2DN=\frac{18}{5}$, and $AE=AD-DE=5-\frac{18}{5}=\boxed{\frac{7}{5}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals AC and BD of the rhombus ABCD intersect at point O. Point E is a point on side AD, and $OD = OE$. If $AC = 8$ and $BD = 6$, then what is the length of AE?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Solution: Draw ON $\perp$ AD at point N. Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, $OD=\frac{1}{2}BD=3$, $OA=\frac{1}{2}AC=4$, and $AC\perp BD$. Therefore, $AD=\sqrt{OA^{2}+OD^{2}}=5$. Since $OD=OE$ and $ON\perp AD$ at point N, $\angle OND=90^\circ$ and $DN=EN$. Also, $S_{\triangle AOD}=\frac{1}{2}AD\cdot ON=\frac{1}{2}OD\cdot OA$, so $5ON=12$, hence $ON=\frac{12}{5}$. Then $DN=\sqrt{OD^{2}-ON^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}-\left(\frac{12}{5}\right)^{2}}=\frac{9}{5}$. Therefore, $DE=2DN=\frac{18}{5}$, and $AE=AD-DE=5-\frac{18}{5}=\boxed{\frac{7}{5}}$.
